body:
## What to build

Bevy screenshot callbacks and readback succeeded in IAB but produced no durable automatic PNG download. An explicit user-activated benchmark canvas button exports real pixels successfully. Diagnose download activation/lifecycle without treating callback success as file durability.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce callback success versus missing file with the tested embedded browser.
- [ ] Export an actual rendered PNG through a supported user action and report failures clearly.
- [ ] Do not introduce character/editor business logic into browser glue.
- [ ] Verify downloaded image dimensions and contents, not only a success log.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Evidence and scope

[M0 verification matrix](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/blob/d74493d/docs/TEST-MATRIX.md); [actual GUI observations](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/blob/d74493d/docs/evidence/GUI-SESSION.md)

Known M0 gap; independent of thin M1.

## 2026-10-12 bounded actual export comparison

VERIFIED — The original current top-level automatic Bevy export and original explicit canvas button both produced durable, independently inspected1280×720 RGB PNGs of the real character/UI (304648 and324903bytes). Download events and current file times match the recorded waits. Startup2's actual Rust callback event is retained separately; callback success alone is not file-durability proof.

PARTIAL — Instrumented iframe A(original unattached/immediate revoke), B(attached/immediate), D(attached/1000ms delayed revoke) and C(original explicit button) made real blob/anchor attempts. No parent-tab download event was observed within the bounded30s/15s total listener windows, and no new matching current file appeared in the narrow Downloads-prefix checks. These are bounded non-observations, not permanent/global absence claims. C had active/trusted tool activation and a real325267-byte canvas PNG; no physical-human click is claimed.

Attachment and delayed revocation did not improve the iframe result. Frame context, hooks and tool/download-session or policy differences remain confounded. The historical top-level missing-file symptom was not reproduced by the current successful controls, so its cause remains UNKNOWN. No workaround or product/dependency/lockfile change is selected. This issue remains OPEN with original criteria retained.

VERIFIED — Five synthetic lifecycle tests and independent agent review; real durable files and actual adapter records are separate evidence. Per-iframe and explicit-button Rust console callback observations and broader-browser/physical-user behavior are NOT-RUN.

[Actual cases and limits](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/blob/5af5f73e5a3a5efe8a07d03b4e51d776b8fc6c26/experiments/25-screenshot-export/REPORT.md), [reproduction](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/blob/5af5f73e5a3a5efe8a07d03b4e51d776b8fc6c26/experiments/25-screenshot-export/README.md), [raw packet](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/blob/5af5f73e5a3a5efe8a07d03b4e51d776b8fc6c26/docs/evidence/bounded-startup-capture/ACCEPTANCE.md), [independent agent review](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/blob/5af5f73e5a3a5efe8a07d03b4e51d776b8fc6c26/docs/evidence/bounded-startup-capture/REVIEW.md); publication [PR #34](https://github.com/Derek-X-Wang/nvwa/pull/34).
title: Make automatic Web screenshot export persist in embedded browsers
